title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Section 49 (Grothendieck's p.550) of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The aim is to study homomorphisms (continuous quotients) of the group M_{0,3}~, as a step toward the general modular groups M_{g,ν}.

Most plausible modern dictionary, consistent with relation (12) on the next page (σ^2 = ρ^3 = 1, σρ = ε_0, ρσ = ε_1):
- \hat{S}^+_{0,3} is the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, i.e. the oriented cartographic group. Its elements ε_0, ε_1, ε_∞ are cusp (inertia) generators.
- M_{0,3}~ is (a version of) its automorphism group. The inner automorphisms form a copy of \hat{S}^+_{0,3}, since the centre is trivial.
- Γ_{0,3}~ is the corresponding outer group. Γ_Q ⊂ Γ_{0,3}~ is the image of Gal(Q̄/Q).
- χ is the cyclotomic-type character (action on cusp/inertia classes, ε_0 ↦ conjugate of ε_0^χ).
- ε_3 is the sign character recording whether ρ goes to a conjugate of ρ or of ρ^{-1}. Equivalently it is χ mod 3, via the action on the 3-part of the abelianisation.

Setup on this page:
- G is a closed subgroup with Inn ≅ \hat{S}^+_{0,3} ⊂ G ⊂ M_{0,3}~. So G is the full preimage of a closed subgroup of Out.
- G is 'big': its image in Out contains an open subgroup of the Galois image Γ_Q.
- For simplicity G ⊂ Ker ε_3, i.e. χ(u) ≡ 1 mod 3.

Consequences:
- In a profinite free product Z/2 * Z/3, every element of order 2 (resp. 3) is conjugate to σ (resp. ρ^{±1}).
- Hence for u ∈ G one can write u(ρ) = int(α_0)ρ and u(σ) = int(β_0)σ, giving maps α_0, β_0 : G → \hat{S}^+_{0,3}. These are the analogues of the Drinfeld/Ihara parameter f in (λ, f) ∈ \hat{GT}, where x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f^{-1} y^λ f.

Next he introduces two subgroups:
- G[0] = G ∩ M~[0], the normaliser in G of the cusp subgroup L_0 = closure of ⟨ε_0⟩.
- G(0), a normalised complement (plausibly: automorphisms fixing σ and sending ε_0 to ε_0^χ).
The resulting structure is:
- G = G(0) · \hat{S}^+ (semidirect product, inner part normal).
- G[0] = G(0) · L_0.
- G[0] ∩ \hat{S}^+ = L_0, i.e. the cusp subgroup is self-normalising in \hat{PSL_2(Z)}.

The next page then pushes everything along a surjection φ: G → M onto a profinite group. It tracks the images of \hat{S}^+, G(0), G[0] and L_0, and the induced maps α, β, presumably to obtain the M_{g,ν} as such quotients/related groups.

The margin note says the whole section is in fact useless, superseded by an interpretation in terms of pro-sets (cf. p. 553'). So this is an abandoned formal setup.
errors: α_0(u), β_0(u) are only determined up to right multiplication by the centralisers ⟨ρ⟩ (order 3) and ⟨σ⟩ (order 2). They are well-defined 'applications' only after a normalisation, which is not stated on this page. They are not homomorphisms but crossed-homomorphism-like maps.
Notational slip: the first line says G ⊂ M_{0,3}, while (1) says G ⊂ M_{0,3}~.

The semidirect product decomposition (4) depends on a precise definition of G(0), presumably given on earlier pages and not reproduced here. Self-normality of L_0 in \hat{PSL_2(Z)}, used in (6), is true but nontrivial in the profinite setting (Herfort–Ribes type results).

ideas.what: Viewing a Galois/GT-type group as a group of automorphisms of \hat{PSL_2(Z)} = (Z/2*Z/3)^ containing all inner automorphisms. Parametrisation by conjugating elements α_0, β_0 for ρ, σ.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps (1997) for braid/PSL_2 versions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses \hat{PSL_2(Z)}/cartographic groups and the Teichmüller tower in general terms; this explicit formalism is not published as far as I know.

ideas.what: Decomposition by the normaliser of a cusp subgroup L_0: G[0] = Norm_G(L_0) = G(0)·L_0 and G = G(0)⋊Inn.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Ihara, Herfort–Ribes for profinite free products)

ideas.what: Studying continuous surjections of such a group onto profinite M, as a route to the modular groups M_{g,ν}.
ideas.modern_name: Quotients/representations of GT-type groups; Teichmüller tower

missed.claim: A programme to derive the general M_{g,ν} from quotients of the automorphism group of \hat{PSL_2(Z)} restricted to Galois-like subgroups. Grothendieck himself abandoned this route in favour of a 'pro-ensembles' interpretation, so it is an abandoned rather than a missed thread.
missed.quote: Toute cette section ... est en fait inutile, à cause de l'interprétation sur des pro-ensembles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest. The pro-set (dessins/cartographic) viewpoint he preferred matches what the later literature developed.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine formal setup (normalised automorphisms of \hat{PSL_2(Z)} with cusp normalisers) closely mirroring known GT formalism, and explicitly declared useless by Grothendieck in the margin.
transcription_corrections: (3): the first line is G(0) = G ∩ M~_{0,3}(0); the second line is \hat G[0] = G ∩ M~_{0,3}[0] = Norm_G(L_0^S).
Margin is approximately: 'Où on se met dans le cadre ... Toute cette section (3 premières sections?) est en fait inutile, à cause de l'interprétation ... pro-ensembles ... dédoublés ... V p. 553''.
(7): 'engendré par ε_0' is an insertion above the line.
